The energy \(E = 3.9\times10^{-6}\,\text{eV}\) corresponds to a frequency  

\[
\nu = \frac{E}{h} \approx \frac{3.9\times10^{-6}\,\text{eV}}{4.1357\times10^{-15}\,\text{eV·s}}
      \approx 9.4\times10^{8}\,\text{Hz}\;(\sim 0.94\ \text{GHz}),
\]

i.e. a radio wavelength of about 32 cm.  
The most well‑known interstellar line at radio frequencies is the 21‑cm hyperfine transition of neutral hydrogen (rest frequency 1.42 GHz, energy ≈ 5.9 µeV). The observed line at ≈ 0.94 GHz is precisely the red‑shifted 21‑cm HI line (requiring \(1+z\approx1.5\), consistent with a distance of ~2 Gpc).

In the Milky Way the 21‑cm line is seen in **absorption** only when the neutral hydrogen is cold (spin temperature ≲ 100 K), because only then is the optical depth high enough to produce an absorption feature against a background continuum source. Warm atomic hydrogen (T ≈ 10⁴ K) emits rather than absorbs at this transition, while molecular transitions lie at much higher energies (mm/sub‑mm). Hence the absorption line is characteristic of the **cold atomic interstellar medium**.

**Answer: C**
